# Actual critical caps can have stationary threshold variance at a free simplex fiber

Criticality alone does not eliminate the threshold-variance phenomenon.
There is an actual convex three-fiber source, a genuine maximum-depth
point, and a fixed family of caps such that:

* every cap passes through that same maximum-depth point and has the
  actual common critical mass;
* each vertex-parallel group covers the entire ambient space;
* a simplex endpoint is freely physically variable under strict actual
  midpoint compatibility;
* its positive normal simplex-volume stress has nonzero threshold
  variance and a negative-definite physical Hessian.

The stationary variation here keeps the other fibers fixed. It does
not assert stationarity under arbitrary simultaneous changes of every
fiber or of the cap parameters. The critical normalized depth is `1/2`,
well above the OC target in this example.

## 1. What a common contact does and does not force

Fix one actual maximum-depth point `(j,y)` with depth `D>0` and with
`y` interior to its positive full-dimensional fiber. If a nonvertical
cap has mass `D` and contains this point, its boundary must pass
through the point. Otherwise moving the boundary parallel up to the
point removes an open slab in the own fiber of positive volume,
contradicting its depth. A cap of mass `D` that excludes the point
has no such implication.

If several such caps have parallel continuous normals at the SELECTED
base `j` and all pass through `(j,y)`, their cuts of that own fiber
coincide. In barycentric vertex coordinates on a simplex at `j`, all
caps with continuous vertex normal `i` have the single threshold
`lambda_i(y)`. Their local threshold variance is therefore zero,
regardless of their different base-normal coefficients.

This conclusion need not hold at another base `p`. A base-normal term
vanishes at `j` but takes different values at `p`, creating different
parallel thresholds there. Nor does a family covering an entire fiber
force its members to pass through a selected point of that fiber.
For one cap per vertex, the barycentric halfspaces `lambda_i>=a_i`
cover their affine span exactly when `sum a_i<=1`; concurrence requires
the stronger equality `sum a_i=1`. These distinctions are respected
by the construction below.

## 2. A centrally symmetric actual source with a free endpoint

Let `K` be a centered `d`-simplex, `d>=2`, with volume `V`, and put

    B=K-K,       U=|B|.

At integer bases `-1,0,1` take the fibers

    K, B, -K.                                                (1)

Their convex hull is a full-dimensional actual convex body with exactly
these integer fibers: the only nontrivial forced midpoint is

    (K+(-K))/2=B/2 subset int B.

This is strict because `0` is interior to the centrally symmetric body
`B`. In particular the endpoint `K` can be replaced by ANY sufficiently
close full-dimensional convex body while `B` and `-K` stay fixed.
For a quantitative justification, choose `rho>0` with `rho Ball subset
B/2`. If `K' subset K+delta Ball`, then

    (K'+(-K))/2 subset B/2+(delta/2)Ball
                        subset (1+delta/(2rho))B/2 subset int B

for `delta<2rho`. Thus the physical simplex paths in the Hessian
calculation really are permissible endpoint variations.

The total mixed mass is `M=2V+U`. The source measure is invariant under
`(z,x)->(-z,-x)`. Consequently its depth at `(0,0)` is at least `M/2`.
Every nonvertical hyperplane through `(0,0)` has zero volume boundary
on every fiber, so either closed side has mass exactly `M/2`.
Two such opposite sides cover the entire ambient space and bound the
depth of every candidate above by `M/2`. Hence the ACTUAL maximum is

    D=M/2=V+U/2,                                            (2)

attained at `(0,0)`, which is interior to the middle fiber. Vertical
closed caps through this point have additional middle-fiber boundary
mass and do not reduce its depth.

## 3. Every endpoint threshold can be globally critical

Write the barycentric coordinates of `K` as

    lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m,     m=d+1,
    sum_i l_i=0,

where the `l_i` are nonzero linear functionals. For ANY proper threshold
`0<a<1`, define the ambient cap

    H_(i,a)={l_i(x)+(a-1/m)z>=0}.                            (3)

It passes through `(0,0)`. On the endpoint `z=-1` it is precisely
`lambda_i(x)>=a`, with mass `(1-a)^d V`. On the reflected endpoint
`z=1`, writing `x=-X` with `X in K`, it becomes `lambda_i(X)<=a`.
The two endpoint masses therefore sum exactly to `V`. On the middle
fiber it is `l_i(x)>=0`, of mass `U/2`. Thus every cap (3) has mass
exactly the common ACTUAL critical budget (2).

If a group has thresholds `a_(g,i)` with `sum_i a_(g,i)=1`, its
ambient linear margins sum to zero. Its `m` caps therefore cover
ALL of `R x R^d`, not merely the endpoint simplex or the mixed source.
They also all pass through the selected maximum-depth point `(0,0)`.

For the nonuniform permutation groups in Section 4, their combined
contact is unique. Two different thresholds in the same continuous
normal give, by subtracting their boundary equations, `z=0`; the
remaining equations `l_i(x)=0` force `x=0`. Thus the full normal family
spans the ambient space, although each individual group has a contact
line. The example does not rely on a rank-deficient combined family.

## 4. A stationary negative-definite free-simplex block

Use the concurrent groups and positive multipliers from
`candidate e25e172f74df55a2`.
They can be chosen in every `d>=2`: group `g` has one threshold
`1-d/(3m)` at vertex `g`, and threshold `1/(3m)` at all other
vertices. Its normalized multipliers `eta=ell(1-a)^d` are

    eta_H=1/(3m^2),        eta_L=(3m-1)/(3m^2 d).

Let `K(W)` be the physically moving endpoint simplex. For every fixed
cap in the family, the two unchanged fibers contribute constants, so
its GLOBAL cap volume satisfies the exact identity

    mu_W(H_(g,i))=D+F_(g,i)(W)-F_(g,i)(I).                   (4)

Its common global budget constraint `mu_W(H_(g,i))<=D` is therefore
EXACTLY the corresponding one-simplex budget
`F_(g,i)(W)<=F_(g,i)(I)`. All cap budgets are equal globally, and all
are active at the baseline.

The global total-volume objective differs from `|K(W)|` by the constant
`U+V`. Thus the positive objective-one stress and the Hessian of the
previous note transfer unchanged to this freely variable endpoint.
With `A` the off-diagonal velocity, column sums `c` and row sums `s`,
the normalized Hessian is

    Q=-[m(4d-7)+1]/[d(3m-1)] ||c||^2
                              -(||s||^2+||A||_F^2)/m.        (5)

This is strictly negative for every nonzero physical simplex velocity.
Its positive multipliers, actual first-order stationarity, and strict
local volume maximum under the fixed GLOBAL cap budgets follow exactly
as in the earlier note. Threshold variance has not disappeared after
requiring an actual critical value, actual compatibility, and a common
maximum-depth contact.

Only the endpoint is varied in this conclusion. In particular (5) is
not a certificate that the whole mixed body is stationary or extremal
when the other fibers and cap parameters may also change.

## 5. Fully rational planar realization

Take `d=2`, `T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)}`, and
`K=T-(1/3,1/3)`. Its area is `V=1/2`. The middle fiber `B=K-K`
is the hexagon with vertices

    (1,0), (0,1), (-1,1), (-1,0), (0,-1), (1,-1),

of area `U=3`. Thus `M=4` and the actual maximum depth is `D=2`.
Use three groups whose endpoint thresholds are the permutations of
`(4/5,1/10,1/10)`, giving each high-threshold cap multiplier `5/6`
and each low-threshold cap multiplier `5/27`. Each group is concurrent;
every one of the nine ambient caps (3) has the same mass `2` and passes
through the middle center. The endpoint Hessian is exactly

    Q=-(11/27)||c||^2-(||s||^2+||A||_F^2)/3,

with inertia `(0,0,6)` and strictly positive objective-one multipliers.
The whole ambient normal family has rank three.

The normalized critical value is `1/2`, whereas the OC target here is
`Gamma_2/2=2/9`. This large gap is material: the example refutes an
unqualified critical-variance exclusion, but supplies no obstruction
specific to a hypothetical near-OC or below-OC extremizer.

The exact verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_actual_critical_threshold_variance.py`
checks every rational cap on every fiber, the whole-space group balance,
strict midpoint slack, the combined rank, and the exact fixed-budget
transfer identity (4) under physical endpoint perturbations.

## 6. Binary embedding: arbitrarily small relative gap above OC as n grows

Keep `d>=2` fixed and denote the critical mass of the three-fiber star
above by `D`, so its total mass is exactly `2D`. For any integer `n>=2`,
write the base as `(z,w)` with `w in R^(n-1)`. At `w=0`, retain the
three original star fibers at `z=-1,0,1`. For every other binary vector
`v in {0,1}^(n-1)`, place a centered simplex of volume `D/Gamma_d`
at EACH of `(0,v)` and `(1,v)`. All simplices may have the same shape
and size. Let the actual body be the convex hull of all these fibers.

Its base projection is

    conv([0,1]^n union {-e_1}).

Every integer base in this projection has binary `w`. A convex
combination projecting to such a binary vector `v` uses only source
points with that same `w=v`, since each coordinate lies in `[0,1]`.
Thus at `v=0` the only integer `z` values are `-1,0,1`; at `v!=0`
they are `0,1`. These are ALL the integer bases. At `v!=0`, the two
endpoint fibers are exact, and at `v=0` the strict midpoint inclusion
already proves exactness of the star middle. Hence the convex hull has
exactly the prescribed full-dimensional integer fibers, is a full
`(n+d)`-dimensional body, and has mixed mass

    M_n=2D+(2^n-2)D/Gamma_d.                                 (6)

Here is an explicit continuation of the critical cap cover. Every star
cap has margin `l_i(x)+(a-1/m)z` on `w=0`. Replace it by

    l_i(x)+(a-1/m)z-L sum_k w_k >=0.

Choose `L` larger than the maximum of the first two terms over the
finitely many other compact fibers. It excludes all of those fibers
strictly, while retaining exactly its original star mass `D` and the
same common star contact. Every original star group still covers the
star fibers; it need not cover the full ambient space after this
component-isolation tilt.

For a regular base `q=(z0,v)`, where `v!=0` is binary and `z0=0` or
`1`, define

    E_v(w)=sum_(v_k=1) w_k-sum_(v_k=0) w_k,
    E_q(z,w)=3 E_v(w)+(2z0-1)z.

This linear functional uniquely maximizes at `q` over the complete
integer support, with gap at least one. Within `w=v` its last term
selects `z0`; another binary `w` loses at least three in the first
term and can gain at most two in the last. A canonical through-centroid
simplex cap `u.x>=0` at `q` is therefore isolated by

    u.x+L_q[E_q(z,w)-E_q(q)]>=0

with `L_q` larger than its maximum `u.x` on every other fiber. Its
global mass is exactly `Gamma_d(D/Gamma_d)=D`. The canonical group
covers the whole own fiber, and these groups cover every regular
component. All these tilts are finite, leave the base coordinates
unchanged, and have strict exclusion margins.

The resulting finite cap family covers the entire actual mixed source
with cap masses all equal to `D`. Hence its maximum depth is at most
`D`. The original star center still has depth at least `D` from the
star alone; every regular own centroid also has depth at least `D`
from its simplex alone. Thus the ACTUAL maximum is exactly `D`.
Each displayed critical cap passes through one of these genuine
maximum-depth points. There are different contact points for the
different components; no common contact for the whole cover is claimed.

The original endpoint remains freely variable: conditioning on the
binary coordinate `w=0` leaves exactly the old strict midpoint
inclusion. All isolated star cap derivatives and the stationary
negative-definite endpoint Hessian remain unchanged. The regular
cover caps strictly exclude that moving endpoint and have constant
mass in its neighborhood.

The ratio between actual maximum depth and the OC target is exactly

    D / (Gamma_d M_n/2^n)
       =2^n/[2^n-2+2Gamma_d] >1,

and tends to one as `n` tends to infinity with `d` fixed. This is an
explicit family ABOVE the OC target, not a counterexample to it. It
shows that a gap depending only on continuous dimension cannot exclude
the existence of this local critical-variance stress by closeness to
the normalized OC target alone.

The cap family is intentionally redundant. Keeping all `m=d+1` star
groups and one canonical group for each of the `2^n-2` regular fibers
uses `2^n+d-1` groups, with possible repeated cap traces. A single star
group would already cover that component; all the star groups are kept
to exhibit the specified variance stress. No minimal-cover property,
necessity of this stress, or reduction to at most `2^n` groups is
asserted. In particular the construction does not rule out arguments
that first select a more restrictive or minimal critical cover.
